cards.title: Controls removed by Option A (1–4)
items: LOST CONTROL — Entra ↔ approved GitHub identity binding: OAuth proves account control, not the employee’s approved login/ID. Risk: wrong or personal account.

LOST CONTROL — coordinated offboarding: today one binding revocation ends admissions/API keys/access; OAuth alone needs separate LiteLLM/GitHub cleanup. Risk: an issued credential can survive disablement.

LOST CONTROL — short-lived bounded admissions: grants expire, limit attempts, bind to catalog/binding revisions and are revocable; direct credentials are not bounded session grants. Risk: a copied credential has a larger reuse window.

LOST CONTROL — expected model catalog reconciliation: CCGC publishes five verified routes and invalidates stale admissions after changes; OAuth alone does not. Risk: stale users/configurations request removed models.

cards.title: Controls removed by Option A (5–8)
items: LOST CONTROL — end-to-end enterprise audit correlation: current audit links Entra ID, immutable GitHub ID, enrollment/API key, admission, model and request. LiteLLM logs alone do not automatically retain this exact corporate chain. Risk: harder incident/compliance evidence.

LOST CONTROL — managed enrollment/account-match approval: CCGC creates users, verifies expected GitHub login, retries and consumes one-time enrollment; native connection is user-driven. Risk: no admin proof of intended person/account.

LOST CONTROL — Claude Code/Desktop managed provisioning: installer backs up settings, manages Keychain/helper, refreshes catalog and configures Desktop Code; OAuth UI does not. Risk: inconsistent endpoint/model/key setup.

LOST CONTROL — API-key/non-interactive user path: CCGC supports enterprise API-key employees and admission exchange without dashboard sessions; native UI does not replace it automatically. Risk: no managed non-interactive lifecycle.
